title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or permission. The person who deployed the system obtained photographs from the victim's private social media account, generated obscene synthetic images, and distributed them across multiple platforms under fake identities to conceal his involvement. The failure was not technical but in the deployment itself: there was no check on who was using the system or what they were generating with it.

What is not established: whether the AI system had safeguards designed to refuse such requests, or whether any platform moderators detected and removed the content before the victim was alerted to its existence by third parties.

The incident shows a person using a widely available tool to conduct targeted harassment and abuse. It required no system failure or technical glitch, only access to an image generation tool and intent to harm. Detection came only when the victim was notified by other users and reported the case to police.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing obscene artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create sexually explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The woman discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts alerting her that her altered photographs and videos were circulating on Discord servers. Police launched an investigation after she filed a complaint at the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Investigators traced digital footprints across the fake profiles and identified Bansal as the perpetrator. During questioning, Bansal admitted he knew the complainant from college and harbored personal resentment toward her. Authorities recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and digital evidence related to the case, with further investigation ongoing.
